messages.author: 236aa224306b9a87
messages.subject: Loading apps from memory
parts:
Hi there,

I'm working to optimize the load time on my apps. Right now, when a user accesses it, it takes about 3-4 seconds for the app to read the .csv file containing the data and then display the graphs via the googleVis package. Say the .csv is automatically generated (by some cron job). I'm aware that the load time can be faster if the .csv file were loaded into memory and kept into memory, so when the user accesses the app, then the app would load the data from memory as opposed to reading from the file. This would likely result in an instantaneous load of the app.

I hope this makes sense. Does anyone have an idea how I can approach this?

Alan

messages.author: 5ab11db47365dff1
messages.subject: Re: Loading apps from memory
parts:
Assuming you have a cronjob hat already dumps the csv data, I'd suggest another cronjob that loads R, processes the new CSV data, and saves an RData file.  

The shiny script then loads the RData file.

Steps

1. Create Rscript file that processes your CSV and saves to RData file (See: http://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/utils/html/Rscript.html)
2. Set up cronjob to execute the Rscript every 10 minutes or whatever makes sense. 
3. Alter your shiny script to load the RData file saved by cron. ....    load(savedData.RData)
4. Profit


Erik

messages.subject: Re: Loading apps from memory

Hi Erik,

Thanks so much for the clear instructions. I went ahead and created an .rds file using saveRDS and subsequently used loadRDS. Unfortunately the load time is just about the same, and this leads me to think that the few seconds' wait is due more in part to the googleVis charts rendering. This would mean it's less of an R/Shiny problem and more of how to get my charts made in googleVis to render more quickly. You wouldn't have an idea around that, would you?

Alan

You can try Joe Cheng package googlevis: https://github.com/jcheng5/googleCharts

Otherwise rCharts https://github.com/ramnathv/rCharts offers most of the functions in the google APIs and more (mainly using open source libraries like D3 etc.).
